sources.name: Long-Term Grazing Density Impacts on Soil Compaction
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Agriculture Agricultural Research Service
source_locators: Six tall-grass prairie paddocks in Oklahoma were rotationally grazed for ten years at 12.5, 25 or 50 cows per hectare; two adjacent ungrazed sites were controls.
Penetration resistance and bulk density increased in the upper 10 centimetres, with significant impact in the high-density treatment.
Surface infiltration fell from 28.5 centimetres per day in ungrazed controls to 7, 5 and 5 centimetres per day under low, moderate and high stocking density.

sources.name: Soil compaction: cattle trampling and grass-yield experiment
sources.publisher: Scotland's Rural College, funded by AHDB Dairy
source_locators: The field experiment compared soil compaction caused by cattle trampling and tractor use with uncompacted grassland and evaluated grass yield and quality.
First-cut grass-silage yield loss reached 19.0 percent under cattle trampling; the larger 37.7-percent tractor result is excluded.
By the third year, the experiment measured a 14.3-percent annual loss of grass dry-matter yield.

metric_contract.unit: infiltration change against local control, cattle stocking density, soil depth and grass-yield loss
metric_contract.geography: six grazed Oklahoma tall-grass prairie paddocks with two adjacent controls; separate SRUC/AHDB grassland field experiment
metric_contract.assessment_period: ten-year USDA grazing treatment and three-year SRUC/AHDB compaction response
metric_contract.boundary: The receipt preserves cattle density, paddock count, control infiltration, soil depth and trial-specific yield results. It does not combine cattle and tractor compaction, infer global prevalence, or treat well-managed dry-soil grazing as overcompaction.

uncertainty: The USDA experiment measures a specific Oklahoma tall-grass prairie system after ten years and the SRUC/AHDB result is a separate grassland trial; neither represents global pasture prevalence. Infiltration change is calculated from source-reported endpoints and is not converted to runoff, erosion or plant-available water volume. The 19-percent yield loss is a maximum first-cut result; tractor compaction and the year-three 14.3-percent annual dry-matter result remain unscored corroboration. Soil texture, moisture, grazing rotation and recovery can materially change outcomes.
